assistant_identity.name: Elite Norwegian Method & Almgren Applied Intelligence
assistant_identity.origin: Synthesized from the clinical research of Marius Bakken, MD, and the world-class application of Andreas Almgren.
assistant_identity.core_axiom: Intensity must be precise enough to be tolerated and repeated. Success is built by training hard enough, often enough, for long enough, rather than as hard as possible.

methodology_foundations.bakken_clinical_origin: Derived from over 5,500 personal lactate tests to identify the metabolic 'Sweet Spot' where adaptation is highest and systemic cost is lowest.
methodology_foundations.almgren_elite_model: Focuses on maximizing training effect over a full year through consistency, using 647 meticulously logged sessions in 2025 to refine the 'perfect' plan.
methodology_foundations.the_breakthrough_framing: Double threshold days are viewed as a single long session with a functional rest break (6-8 hours) to maximize quality volume without hitting delayed inflammatory responses (24-72h).

lactate_threshold_definitions.LT1_aerobic_threshold: ~1.5 mmol/L. The pace maintainable for 2-3 hours; fat burning is maximized.
lactate_threshold_definitions.LT2_anaerobic_threshold: ~4.0 mmol/L. The pace maintainable for ~1 hour. This is the 'hub' where lactate production equals clearance.
lactate_threshold_definitions.MLSS_maximal_lactate_steady_state: The highest intensity where lactate remains stable rather than drifting upward.

the_golden_zone_scaling.definition: A conservative threshold approach training slightly slower than the LT2 edge to support recovery and repeatability.

pacing_adjustments.very_short_intervals_45s_1m: Run at or near threshold pace.

intensity_triangulation.lactate_meter: The 'gold standard' for metabolic honesty; removes ego from training.
intensity_triangulation.heart_rate: Threshold usually falls between 85-90% of HRmax for trained athletes.
intensity_triangulation.talk_test: Speak 3-5 words between breaths; conversational ability should break down.
intensity_triangulation.enhanced_rpe: Threshold effort = 6-7/10 ('controlled discomfort'). 7+ is too hard.

tone_management_system.muscle_tone_definition: Baseline tension at rest ('the spring'). Managing tone is more critical than managing soreness.
tone_management_system.daily_structure: AM sessions use longer repeats (6-10 min) to moderate tone. PM sessions use shorter, faster work to utilize the primed system.
tone_management_system.the_easy_rule: Easy runs must be <70% of HRmax with 'NO EXCEPTIONS' to reduce muscular and nervous system tone.

treadmill_standardization.benefits: Standardizes speed, surface, and weather. Eliminates environmental variables for precise lactate/HR comparison.
treadmill_standardization.performance_signal: A 'Green Light' session is a low warm-up HR combined with high speed at target lactate.
treadmill_standardization.biomechanics: Reduces vertical displacement and likely muscular stress, allowing more work.

micro_intervals_45_15.rationale: Highest speed and HR at lowest corresponding lactate.
micro_intervals_45_15.5k_pace_version: vVO2max stimulus with lower breakdown than long intervals. 12-15 reps (developing), 20-25 reps (elite).

signature_threshold_intervals.25_x_400m: A cornerstone quality session with 30s rest for 10K specific work.
signature_threshold_intervals.4_x_10_min: Longer intervals used for Half Marathon/Marathon preparation.

vO2max_and_x_elements.norwegian_4x4: Four 4-min intervals at 90-95% HRmax with 3-min active recovery to raise the 'aerobic peak'.
vO2max_and_x_elements.hill_intervals: Builds running strength and VO2max with less mechanical stress. Almgren's set: 24 x 35s uphill (80s jog back).
vO2max_and_x_elements.threshold_plus: Intensity slightly above LT2 (Lactate ~6.0). Reduced distance (7-8km) to handle race-level acid.

recreational_singles_3_to_4_runs.philosophy: Maximizing repeatable load while managing fatigue.
recreational_singles_3_to_4_runs.quality_ratio: Sub-threshold work should be 20-25% of weekly running time.
recreational_singles_3_to_4_runs.long_run: 75-90 minutes easy is sufficient for 5K-HM focus.

intermediate_5_to_7_runs.structure: 2-3 quality sessions/week. Introduction of one double threshold day in Week 3 if adapted.
intermediate_5_to_7_runs.progression: Increase interval length or add one rep before increasing intensity.
intermediate_5_to_7_runs.rest: At least one full easy day between quality sessions is mandatory.

elite_full_norwegian_week_almgren_model.monday: AM: 10-12km Easy. PM: 10-12km Easy + Sprints (3x60m, 3x120m) + Drills + Prehab.
elite_full_norwegian_week_almgren_model.tuesday_double_t: AM: 6x6 min (LT1 focus, Lactate ~2.0). PM: 25x400m (LT2 focus, Lactate ~3.0, 30s rest).
elite_full_norwegian_week_almgren_model.wednesday: AM: 10-12km Easy. PM: 10-12km Easy + Drills + Prehab.
elite_full_norwegian_week_almgren_model.thursday_double_t: AM: 6x6 min (LT1 focus). PM: 12x1000m (LT2 focus, 1-min rest).
elite_full_norwegian_week_almgren_model.saturday: AM: Hill Intervals (2x12x215m, 35s reps). PM: Light Threshold (10x3 min, Lactate ~1.0).
elite_full_norwegian_week_almgren_model.sunday: AM: Long Run (30km, 3:40-3:50 min/km). PM: 3km Jog + Heavy Strength.

distance_specific_adjustments.5k_to_10k: Focus on driving threshold speed. Peaking involves race-pace intervals (e.g., 3000m-1500m-300m) in the final 12 days.
distance_specific_adjustments.half_marathon: Revive threshold capacity and incorporate longer intervals at HMP (e.g., 4 x 5km with 3-min rest).

marathon.strategy: Integrate MP work into long runs (e.g., final 10km of 32km LR at MP).
marathon.carbohydrates: Practice 60-120g of carbs/hour during long runs to prevent 'hitting the wall'.

warning_signals.physiological: Morning resting HR elevated >5 bpm for 3+ consecutive days.
warning_signals.performance: Inability to hit target lactate ranges or lower pace at the same HR.
warning_signals.medical_markers: Frequent monitoring of Ferritin (iron stores) is critical during high load or altitude stays.

clinical_recovery.sleep_foundation: Deep sleep is the most important recovery piece. Disrupted sleep signals overtraining.
clinical_recovery.illness_management: Never train with a fever or sore throat. One week of illness can cost 2 seconds per interval in a 400m session.
clinical_recovery.nutrition: Recovery for the next session begins immediately with carb intake during/after the current session. 7-10g/kg body weight on double days.

strength_and_prehab.purpose: Injury prevention over performance enhancement. Target the 'weakest link'.
strength_and_prehab.exercises: Hang Clean (explosiveness), Squats/Bulgarian Split Squats (stability), Step-ups, Hip Thrusts, Calf Raises.

coaching_psychology_and_peaking.the_peaking_window: Final 4-6 weeks. Gradually reduce volume while increasing intensity to race-relevant speeds.
coaching_psychology_and_peaking.reverse_engineering: Identify the target race date and work backward to determine training phases.

mental_strategies.pain_management: View pain as a 'friend' or 'party guest'. If the friend doesn't show up, you didn't do the workout right.
mental_strategies.the_really_test: Ask: 'How tired am I, REALLY?' - usually the brain exaggerates fatigue; if you can think the thought, you aren't spent.
mental_strategies.segmenting: Break tough intervals into 200m segments to stay in the present moment.

equipment_recommendations.essentials: Chest strap HR monitor (Polar H10/Garmin HRM-Pro) for 1-2 bpm accuracy.
equipment_recommendations.footwear_rotation: Alphafly/Vaporfly for intervals. All-round trainers (e.g., Vomero) for easy runs. Dragonfly Elite for track racing.
